external_primary_research_delta.title: Where Steering Signals Come From: Activation Source Selection in Activation Steering
external_primary_research_delta.authors: Jiaran Ye, Lingxu Ran, Zijun Yao, Chenpeng Wang, Yong Jiang, Lei Hou, Juanzi Li, Liangming Pan
external_primary_research_delta.reported_finding_scope: Holding downstream intervention fixed, changing source context/readout policy substantially changes steering success across the reported models/tasks. Strong signals are reported near execution-boundary states where the model is about to realize the target behavior; tail subtraction is proposed to remove shared prompt/continuation semantics and improve stability.
external_primary_research_delta.project_effect: Global J-Space evaluation must treat steering-vector SOURCE POLICY as an explicit experimental factor. A readable semantic direction extracted from arbitrary states is insufficient. For Xeno/EntityOS cognitive-process control, compare process-execution-boundary states against target-appearance and generic semantic states before attributing causal control to a J-Space direction.
external_primary_research_delta.evidence_ceiling: Does not prove the same source policy works for Qwen3.5-0.8B or Clay/Xeno; requires exact-checkpoint model-specific replication.

external_primary_research_delta.title: Belief Dynamics Reveal the Dual Nature of In-Context Learning and Activation Steering
external_primary_research_delta.reported_finding_scope: The reported framework models context and activation interventions as distinct ways of shifting latent concept beliefs, predicting nonlinear behavioral transitions and interaction effects.
external_primary_research_delta.project_effect: Do not assume BIND/ROUTE and WRITE/STEER are interchangeable channels. Trigger-2 should evaluate context evidence accumulation and vector intervention separately and jointly, with preregistered interaction tests.
external_primary_research_delta.evidence_ceiling: Framework-level donor only; no Clay/Qwen-specific causal promotion.

external_primary_research_delta.title: Does learning the right latent variables necessarily improve in-context learning?
external_primary_research_delta.reported_finding_scope: The reported experiments find that extracting task-relevant latent variables can succeed while downstream use of those latents still fails to improve robust out-of-distribution prediction.
external_primary_research_delta.project_effect: Strengthens the current separation READ != BIND/ROUTE != WRITE/CONTROL. Decodability of a Hyperposition/J-Space state is not enough; downstream use and variable-N/OOD transfer need separate acceptance metrics.
external_primary_research_delta.evidence_ceiling: General method input only; not Qwen3.5-specific evidence.

new_hypothesis.claim: For a reusable 0.8B Xeno cognitive-process substrate, J-Space control vectors extracted from states immediately before an intended cognitive transition may transfer more reliably across variable-N/process contexts than vectors extracted merely from states where the target concept is semantically present.
new_hypothesis.finished_xeno_relevance: The finished Xeno must coordinate process execution, DB-vs-simulation decisions, handoff/re-entry and Hyperposition updates. A carrier that tracks 'about to execute this process transition' is more directly aligned with those functions than static concept readability if the hypothesis survives model-specific causal tests.

counterhypotheses.claim: Execution-boundary superiority may be specific to larger instruction-tuned models/tasks and may disappear or reverse in the target approximately-0.8B checkpoint.
Tail subtraction or aggressive semantic subtraction may remove functionally required process-state information in a small model, reducing control even if it improves directional purity metrics.

Some model-visible role-typed ClayCode/Typed-Entry fields are causally authoritative for the process transition; forcing invariance to them would damage the intended computation rather than remove a shortcut.
